_meta.description: Calibration anchors for set_population: credible published estimates of Pokemon TCG print runs, graded-population totals, or packs sold. Used to calibrate and sanity-check the relative-population model (graded_pop / popularity). See docs/prior_art.md for methodology and citations.

credibility_legend.official: Published by The Pokemon Company / WotC, or directly derived from an official figure.
credibility_legend.well-sourced-estimate: Hobbyist/analyst estimate built on a documented chain of reasoning and at least one verifiable input (pop report, official checkpoint, pull rate).
credibility_legend.hobbyist-guess: Round number with no documented derivation; treat as a weak prior only.

_meta.warning: A wrong anchor poisons calibration worse than a missing one. Several values below are explicitly flagged hobbyist-guess. Do NOT hard-anchor on those; use them only for order-of-magnitude sanity checks. The graded_pop_total anchors are the most reliable (directly countable from pop reports) but are NOT print runs -- grading rate is exactly the popularity bias the project is trying to correct for, so they are an endogenous cross-check, not a ground-truth divisor.
_meta.set_id_convention: Matches dim_sets in the main repo. base1=Base, base2=Jungle, base3=Fossil, base4=Base Set 2, base5=Team Rocket, gym1=Gym Heroes, gym2=Gym Challenge, neo1=Neo Genesis, neo2=Neo Discovery, neo3=Neo Revelation, neo4=Neo Destiny, ex7=Team Rocket Returns.

anchors.notes: Official 'Pokemon in Figures' cumulative total: 75 billion cards printed worldwide since 1996, as of end of FY2024-25 (Mar 2025). This is the single hardest anchor available -- it caps the sum of all per-set estimates. ~44.6B (60%) printed since FY2020-21, confirming production is heavily back-loaded to the modern era.

Official cumulative checkpoint: 23.6B through Mar 2017. Useful as an upper bound for the SUM of all WOTC + early-modern sets. Other official checkpoints: ~43.2B (Mar 2022), 52.9B (Mar 2023), 64.9B (Mar 2024). Annual: 9.7B (FY22), 11.9B (FY23, record), 10.2B (FY24).

12 billion CUMULATIVE cards printed end of 2001 (an official-ish checkpoint cited in the Elite Fourum thread), NOT Neo Revelation alone. Listed under neo3 because Neo Revelation (Sep 2001) is the set straddling that checkpoint. Per-set average implied by the thread: ~1.2B/set across the WOTC era. Do not read 12B as a single-set figure. 1st Edition Base is the smallest WOTC run -- printed in a very short window (WotC FAQ cited as '3 days') before Pokemania peaked. Elite Fourum derives ~10% of Base Set total as 1st Ed. Wide band: the popular '100,000 1st-Edition Charizards printed' figure (ogcards.com) has no documented source. The number here is total cards in the SET, not just Charizard. Treat as order-of-magnitude only. [UNIT CORRECTION 2026-07-21: provenance traced to gottaketchumall's 2018-05-08 Elite Fourum thread - these are ALL-LANGUAGES 'wild ass guesses' calibrated to sum to the 12B end-2001 checkpoint, under an assumed 50/50 English/non-English split. As English-only anchors they must be roughly HALVED. https://www.elitefourum.com/raw/20273/2]

1st Edition Base Charizard (#4) graded population across all companies = 6,115 (PSA 4,484 incl. 125 PSA-10; BGS thick 405 + thin 724; CGC 502). This is ONE card, not the whole set. Inflated by crack-and-resubmit. The article estimates <10,000 surviving copies of the Charizard. Use as a per-chase-card pop anchor, exactly the kind of signal the project's chase_graded_pop.json will collect.

Shadowless Base Charizard (#4) graded pop = 13,885 (PSA 10,635 incl. 58 PSA-10; CGC 1,571; BGS 1,679). Article estimates ~15,000+ surviving. One card. Note shadowless is rarer than Unlimited but more common than 1st Ed -- and shadowless graded pop > 1st-Ed graded pop, consistent with that ordering. Good ratio anchor: shadowless ~2.3x 1st-Ed Charizard graded pop.

~$500M of WOTC's $669M 1999 revenue was Pokemon TCG (worldwide, all languages, wholesale). Derivation: Hasbro 8-K Q4 $237-271M + $398M pro-forma pre-acquisition delta = $669M WOTC total; minus ~$155M 1998 WOTC baseline = $514M; trimmed to $450-470M since Magic also grew. Covers Base/Jungle/Fossil retail window. Converting to cards needs 1999 wholesale pack pricing (open question). [deep-research 2026-07-21, 3-0, SEC-verified inputs]

AUDITED-FILING-DERIVED: Pokemon trading card line = 15% of Hasbro FY2000 net revenues $3,787.2M => ~$568M wholesale (worldwide, all languages). Peak-era window: Base Set 2/Team Rocket/Gym/Neo Genesis. ICv2 independently computes same figure. [deep-research 2026-07-21, 3-0]

FY2001: no product line above 10% of $2,856.3M => OFFICIAL ceiling $286M; quantified declines (~$469M Games-segment Pokemon drop) imply actual ~$100M or less. Filing also cites obsolescence writeoffs from 'overproduction of certain trading card games, primarily POKEMON related' - direct official evidence late-WOTC sets were overprinted vs sell-through. Window: Neo Discovery/Revelation + carryover. [deep-research 2026-07-21, 3-0]

'Over 20 billion shipped' appears in TPCi press-release boilerplate June 2013 - March 2014 (immewnity, press-release email archive, elitefourum post 71). Floor value; midpoint of window used as date. [forum re-read 2026-07-21]

Independent derivation from audited Hasbro SEC revenue (see conversion_evidence.wotc_revenue_to_cards). Cross-validates the 12B-global x 0.40-EN-share = ~4.8B path. [deep-research + sourcing 2026-07-21]

qualitative_constraints.ordinal_era_ranking: DP < HGSS < BW (single-poster, uncorroborated); early XY < late XY; late SM considerably lower than early SM (corroborated: 2021 Cosmic Eclipse reprint forced by $200+ boxes); SWSH 'uber printed' (corroborated: official 9.7-11.9B/yr vs ~1.5-2B/yr pre-2019). Inconsistent with holding DP=HGSS=BW=200M equal.
qualitative_constraints.shadowless_vs_1st_ed_ratio: Bare-guess prior only: 0.5x to 2.33x Shadowless:1stEd. The 30%-of-first-print-is-1E 'industry standard' is secondhand Konami hearsay, disputed in-thread by seller data suggesting Shadowless may be RARER than 1st Ed. No WOTC-specific evidence exists.
qualitative_constraints.wotc_per_set_1e: NEGATIVE FINDING (protective): no statistically conclusive 1st Edition/Shadowless/Unlimited per-set figures exist anywhere as of 2026; all circulating numbers incl. our base1-1E-1.5M are bare guesses. Skyridge 'single print run' story is [citation needed] on Bulbapedia with no primary documentation.
qualitative_constraints.modern_capacity: 2025 global production (~10B/yr) = pre-expansion capacity ceiling (TPCi max-capacity statements + TPC 2026 demand-outpaced-capacity admission); 2025 sets share a fixed pie. Millennium Print Group's 1.27M sqft Morrisville NC lease (largest US mfg lease of 2025) implies ~2x capacity from late 2027-2028; do NOT extrapolate the 2025 plateau past 2027.
qualitative_constraints.followups: 1) English-vs-non-English share by era is THE unresolved scaling assumption. 2) 1999-2001 wholesale pack pricing would convert the three SEC revenue anchors to card counts. 3) elitefourum thread 63246 (2010-2020 print runs) should be re-read for later numeric posts - the claim that it contains none was REFUTED 0-3 in verification.

booster_msrp_wotc.notes: WOTC's own store, Dec 2000: Neo Genesis 1E boosters $3.29, sealed box $118.44 = exactly 36x3.29. Street price often $2.99 (Arizona Daily Wildcat, Oct 1999); WOTC itself cleared old sets at $2.00 late-2000, so realized $/pack < MSRP late-cycle.

cards_per_pack.notes: 11 cards/pack Base through Neo Destiny; drops to 9 for e-Card and EX series. Japanese packs 5 cards.

wholesale_fraction_of_msrp.notes: Hobby-trade convention: distributors pay ~40% of MSRP, direct retailers ~50%. ICv2 (Dec 2001, WOTC-sourced) shows much Pokemon volume went DIRECT to chains/retailers, so blended realization 40-55% of MSRP is defensible. No Pokemon-specific wholesale % exists anywhere (searched: trade press, court filings).

english_share_of_global.notes: No official language share exists. Evidence (INDIRECT - retail VALUE not print volume; Japan figure covers ALL card games; JP packs hold 5 cards vs 11 EN, so value parity only loosely constrains unit share): Japan card-game market ~$1.9B FY2024 ~ same order as US Pokemon retail (Circana >$1B); production split TPCi (Western langs) vs TPC (Japan/Asia); language count grew 11 (2015) -> 13 (2020) -> 16 (2026), diluting EN. WOTC-era cross-check: 12B global end-2001 x 0.40 = 4.8B EN vs independent SEC-revenue derivation 4.2-7.4B EN (1999-2001) - two paths agree. Central 0.40 pre-2020, 0.35 post-2020, +/-0.10 band propagated to sensitivity.

wotc_revenue_to_cards.derivation: cards = revenue / (wholesale_frac x 3.29 USD/pack) x 11 cards/pack. CY1999 $450-514M -> 2.7-4.3B; CY2000 $549-587M -> 3.4-4.9B; CY2001 $50-286M -> 0.3-2.4B (all WOTC-western-languages). English at 0.65 (0.50-0.80) of WOTC-west -> 1999-2001 English total ~4.2-7.4B.
